chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is not fitting for anyone to raise a structure above the structure of the Ka'ba." And whoever takes something of the dust of the House and what is around the Ka'ba, he must return it to its place. It was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking dust from the Ka'ba?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the Ka'ba's unique status as the highest point of honor in sacred architecture, prohibiting any structure from surpassing its height to preserve its visual and spiritual supremacy. It further emphasizes the sanctity of the site by mandating the restitution of any taken earth, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the physical elements of the Haram carry inherent reverence and must be treated with care to avoid desecration.
